config.title: Write a toggle visibility widget

intro.title: Write a toggle visibility widget
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple toggle visibility widget that shows or hides a piece of content, like a paragraph or image, when a button is clicked. You will learn the core programming concept of state management using a boolean variable to track whether the content is visible or hidden. The main technologies involved are JavaScript for handling click events and DOM manipulation to update the webpage dynamically. By the end, you will have a functional widget that demonstrates how to control element visibility interactively.
intro.usecase: The toggle visibility pattern is a fundamental building block for interactive user interfaces. You'll use it to create collapsible sections in dashboards, expandable menus in navigation bars, and show/hide panels for filters or settings. For example, a user might click a 'Details' button to reveal additional form fields or a 'Filters' button to display advanced search options. Mastering this pattern allows you to build clean, space-efficient interfaces that respond to user actions.

objectives: Initialize a state variable to control the visibility of a UI element
Construct a handler function that toggles the state value between true and false
Bind the handler function to a button's click event to trigger the toggle
Manipulate the DOM to conditionally render content based on the current visibility state
Integrate the state, handler, and conditional rendering into a single functional component
Apply inline styles or CSS classes to visually indicate the current visibility state
Configure the component to update the UI dynamically in response to user interaction

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a library
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the ToggleVisibility component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ToggleVisibility that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name ToggleVisibility and have it return null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ToggleVisibility component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The ToggleVisibility component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: A component named ToggleVisibility exists and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the component is named exactly 'ToggleVisibility' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named ToggleVisibility that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize visibility state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your ToggleVisibility component, add a useState hook to create a state variable named 'isVisible' and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Call useState(false) and destructure the returned array into isVisible and setIsVisible.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'isVisible' initialized to false, ready to control visibility.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'isVisible' and initializes it to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've correctly initialized the state variable to false and named it 'isVisible'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState(false) and destructure it into [isVisible, setIsVisible].

steps.title: Define the toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your ToggleVisibility component, define a function called toggleVisibility that toggles the isVisible state between true and false.
steps.hint: You can define the function using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Inside the function, use the setter function from useState to update the state to the opposite of its current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a toggleVisibility function that uses the setter function to toggle the isVisible state.
successCriteria: A toggleVisibility function is defined inside the component that toggles the isVisible state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggleVisibility function properly toggles the isVisible state value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleVisibility function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's inside the component and properly toggles the state.

steps.title: Add a container div to the component return
steps.instruction: In your ToggleVisibility component, replace the current return value (null) with a div element to serve as the container for your widget.
steps.hint: Return a JSX div element instead of null. This will be the main wrapper for your widget content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element that will contain the toggle widget elements.
successCriteria: The component returns a JSX div element instead of null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element instead of null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element to serve as the container for the widget.

steps.title: Add a heading to the container
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an h1 element with the text 'Toggle Visibility Widget'.
steps.hint: Add the h1 element as a child of the container div you created in the previous step.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display a heading inside the container div.
successCriteria: The container div contains an h1 element with the exact text 'Toggle Visibility Widget'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a heading to your widget container.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a heading, but check the text content or element placement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Make sure you're adding an h1 element with the specified text inside the container div.

steps.title: Conditionally render content based on state
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays 'Content is visible!' only when the isVisible state variable is true. Use a ternary operator for conditional rendering.
steps.hint:
You can use a ternary operator: {isVisible ?

Content is visible!

: null}. Place this after your heading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now conditionally display the paragraph 'Content is visible!' only when isVisible is true.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with the text 'Content is visible!' is conditionally rendered using a ternary operator that checks the isVisible state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using a ternary operator to conditionally render the paragraph based on the isVisible state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering isn't quite right. Check that you're using a ternary operator with isVisible and rendering the paragraph only when it's true.

steps.title: Add the toggle button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Toggle Visibility' inside the container div, and wire its onClick event to call the toggleVisibility handler function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with an onClick attribute that references your toggleVisibility function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Visibility' appears in the UI, and clicking it will toggle the visibility of the paragraph content.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Toggle Visibility' is added to the container div, and its onClick event is wired to the toggleVisibility handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Toggle Visibility' and its onClick attribute is set to call the toggleVisibility function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected. Ensure you add a <button> element with onClick={toggleVisibility} and the text 'Toggle Visibility' inside the container div.

steps.title: Display current visibility status
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph below the heading that displays the current value of the isVisible state variable. For example, show 'Visibility: true' or 'Visibility: false'.
steps.hint:
You can add a

tag and use curly braces to embed the isVisible value in the text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a state value

Current value: {someState}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current visibility status (true/false) in a paragraph below the heading.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays the text 'Visibility: ' followed by the current isVisible value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it shows the actual isVisible value (not just static text).
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph showing the visibility status is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the ToggleVisibility component as the default export so it can be imported and used in other files.
steps.hint: Add 'export default ToggleVisibility;' at the end of the file, after the component definition.
steps.analogousExample:
// Exporting a component for use elsewhere
export default MyComponent;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component is exported and ready to be imported into other modules.
successCriteria: ToggleVisibility is exported as the default export
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're exporting the component as the default export.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component needs to be exported. Add 'export default ToggleVisibility;' at the end of the file.
